q: Day 6 branches into three tracks. What decides which track a learner follows?
options: Their own work situation — jobseekers, NGO/programme staff, or teachers
How much money they paid for the course
Which day of the week they started
explanation: The lesson branches by role: Track A for jobseekers and professionals, Track B for NGO and programme staff, Track C for teachers and lecturers. Each learner follows the one that matches their real work.

q: In the job-scam check, which of these is a definite red flag?
options: The employer asks you to pay a recruitment or training fee
The interview is scheduled for a weekday
The job description asks for two years of experience
explanation: No genuine employer charges you to apply, pays for training materials, or collects any fee at all. Any recruitment fee means walk away — and verify the company registration separately.

q: What is the correct way to use AI when drafting a proposal section against a donor's call?
options: Let the AI invent activities and figures to make the proposal look bigger
Paste the donor's language and rewrite your draft using it — without inventing activities or figures you do not have
Copy another organisation's proposal and change the name
Ask the AI to write the whole proposal from its own imagination
explanation: AI should match your draft to the donor's own priority language — but every activity and figure must come from your real plan. AI proposes; you decide and verify.

q: A teacher asks AI for revision questions with answers. What must happen before those answers are taught?
options: Nothing — AI answers are always correct for school topics
The teacher verifies each answer using the Day 2 four-question check
The students check each other's answers
The answers are printed as they are
explanation: The Day 2 verification check is not optional in a classroom. AI generates plausible-but-wrong answers often enough that every answer must be checked before it reaches students.
